_comment: ESP32-WROVER-E-N16R8: classic ESP32-D0WD-V3 die, 16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM.
Project-local because nothing shipped describes it. esp-wrover-kit is the
FTDI development kit with 4 MB of flash and a debug probe; upesy_wrover is
a different board with a different variant directory. Both would declare
the wrong flash size and the wrong upload tooling.
variant stays "esp32" -- the generic classic-ESP32 pin variant. A WROVER-E
module has the same bonded-out pins as a WROOM-32D except that GPIO16 and
GPIO17 are committed to the PSRAM chip, and that is a firmware pin-map
question rather than a core variant question. See hw_config.h.
extra_flags deliberately does NOT include -mfix-esp32-psram-cache-issue.
The stock WROVER manifests do, and for an ESP32 revision below 3 they must:
the cache erratum is real on that silicon. A WROVER-E carries the D0WD-V3
die, revision 3, where it is fixed -- so the barriers cost throughput on
the audio path and IRAM in the image for a bug this part does not have.
This is checked rather than assumed: board_caps_begin() reads the chip
revision at boot and marks the board degraded if it is below 3, because
un-barriered code touching PSRAM on that silicon is genuinely unsafe.
-DBOARD_HAS_PSRAM is what the Arduino core and the libraries look at to
decide whether ps_malloc() is real. It is not what enables PSRAM: that is
CONFIG_SPIRAM=y in the precompiled framework libraries, which is already
set for every esp32 build, with psramInit() running from a system init
hook and psramAddToHeap() from initArduino(). One flag alone was never
the whole story here.
name: ESP32-WROVER-E-N16R8 (16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM)
